title: Three Autumns and One Short Jar
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：garlic　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 garlic 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the cook ① planted garlic that no neighbour in the court would have described, and he said the planting was the whole of the autumn. The ② garlic, meaning the bulbs themselves and not the leaves, ran three autumns and stayed undescribed in the book; garlic, he said, is the only thing in a court that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ head of garlic in that court had the same short jar beside it, and the ④ garlic at the far shelf, meaning the bulbs they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Garlic, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the cook said the describing is the part that fills three autumns.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the garlic was the whole of the matter, meaning the flavour and not the bulbs. The ⑥ garlic, meaning the flavour and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; garlic, he said, is either something you plant or the only word that means both a bulb and a flavour. He said the flavour is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ garlic had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short jar. The ⑧ garlic of the whole thing, the cook wrote in November, was one court and three autumns of describing; garlic, he said, is either the bulbs at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ garlic I remember is the garlic described in the plan, which closed in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the court. ⑩ Garlic, my mother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being described; all garlic, she said, is a flavour that has agreed to look like a bulb. She said the flavour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 大蒜（指院子里每一头旁边的那一头）
B. n. 大蒜（指那些蒜头本身，与蒜叶相对）
C. 固定搭配：plant garlic 种蒜
D. n. 大蒜（指留给孩子们的那些蒜头）
E. n. 大蒜（抽象总称，指一个院子的种蒜之事）
F. n. 大蒜（指清单里写到、被称过的那些）
G. n. 蒜味；蒜香（指一件事里人人都闻却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 蒜味（抽象总称，指人人都闻却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: planted garlic that no neighbour in the court would have described

answers.why: plant garlic 意为“种蒜”，1965 年那位厨师种了院子里没有一位邻居肯描述的大蒜。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，指那些蒜头本身而不是蒜叶，它经过了三个秋天而在簿子上没有被描述。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，指院子里每一头旁边的那一头，每一头旁边都有同一只矮矮的罐子。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，指最远架子上留给孩子们的那些蒜头，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
garlic 意为“蒜味、蒜香”，指一件事里人人都闻却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这股蒜味就是那件事的全部。
garlic 意为“蒜味”，指人人都闻却无人提起的那样东西而不是那些大蒜，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，指清单里写到、被称过的那些，到 1971 年这些成了计划里的一行。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，厨师十一月写道，整件事的种蒜之事是一个院子和三个秋天的描述。
garlic 意为“大蒜”，我记得的是计划里描述过的那些，1973 年用完了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一批。
garlic 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，大蒜是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
